papers.title: Elastic polar oscillations and nuclear parameters
papers.abstract: Owing to the elasticity of a neutron star, the shear and interface modes are excited, in addition to the fundamental, pressure, and gravity modes. While direct observations of the oscillation spectrum remain challenging, potential resonance signatures from these modes could be manifested in the precursors of short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron star mergers. If the oscillation spectrum is observed, this is a good opportunity to extract the physical properties through the technique of asteroseismology. In particular, we focus on the crustal elasticity and examine the $s$- and $i$-mode frequencies. We find that, for a given EOS specified by the nuclear saturation parameters, the radius-scaled $s$-mode frequencies and the mass-scaled $i$-mode frequencies can be expressed as a function of the stellar compactness, independently of the stiffness of the core EOS, at least when the EOS in a higher-density region can be characterized only by the specific constant sound velocity. Then, we could derive the fitting formula for the $s_i$-mode for $i=1-4$ and $i_1$-mode frequencies as a function of the stellar compactness and the combination of the incompressibility of symmetric nuclear matter, $K_0$, and the slope parameter for the nuclear symmetry energy, $L$. If the $s$- and/or $i$-mode oscillation frequencies were observed, one may get the relation between these properties by identifying the observed frequencies with specific modes, using our fitting formula, which offers useful insights into the nuclear saturation parameters and stellar properties. By combining the other observational data, it may be possible to narrow the parameter space of EOS parameters and stellar properties. We emphasize that this article summarizes the results presented in our previous studies and discusses their implications for neutron star seismology.

papers.title: Analyzing Fermionic Dark Matter Scenarios with Anomalous Compact Objects
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider three compact objects (HESS J1731-347, PSR J1231-1411, XTE J1814-338) with anomalous mass-radius relations to analyze the possibility of their being dark matter admixed neutron stars. We try to infer the properties of the dark matter particles, under the assumption of behaving as a free Fermi gas. The main novelty relies on the use of a baryonic equation of state obtained from first principles over the whole density range, which allows the model dependence of the baryonic part of the calculation to be eliminated. Once the possible dark matter admixed neutron star configurations are obtained, we check their stability and whether it is feasible for a neutron star to capture the necessary dark matter fraction. Our analysis shows that our dark matter model favours the dark matter admixed neutron star hypothesis over the pure baryonic neutron star one, with the most favoured dark matter mass of $m_{DM} = 1$~GeV, although the necessary dark matter content cannot be explained in a standard galactic environment.

papers.title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
papers.abstract: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.

papers.title: Nuclear deep-inelastic scattering as a BSM probe via SMEFT
papers.abstract: Searches for New Physics at the energy frontier have motivated theoretical development of model-independent methods to constrain interactions beyond the Standard Model (BSM) like the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), as well as associated phenomenological analyses. While these approaches are powerful, they are also afflicted by the large space of higher-dimensional operators and the challenge of possible degeneracies among these operators. To help ameliorate these difficulties, processes beyond those at hadron colliders, including deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), have been identified and studied for their ability to contribute added constraining power. In this work, we extend such investigations to charged-lepton DIS involving heavy nuclei, for which we explore the systematics of SMEFT effects for a series of representative cases. In particular, we point out that nuclear effects can reshuffle the luminosities governing partons entering SMEFT-corrected hard interactions, such that the nucleus can serve as an expanded laboratory to explore SMEFT effects complementary to free-nucleon DIS. In particular, we find that nuclear DIS possesses significant constraining power over flavor-isovector SMEFT operator combinations, with reduced nPDF dependence; similarly, improved control over nPDFs would further enhance the SMEFT reach of nuclear DIS observables. We explore projections for future (proposed) facilities like the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh, finding that improvements to nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) can further sharpen the reach of nuclear DIS.

papers.title: Gluon GPDs from hard-exclusive electroproduction of heavy quarkonium at NLO
papers.abstract: Gluon tomography of the nucleon through hard-exclusive electroproduction of $J/\psi$ has been one of the key motivations for Electron-Ion Collider. However, the next-to-leading order (NLO) perturbative QCD calculations available in the literature were performed either in the collinear factorization limit where the heavy-quark mass is neglected, or in heavy-quark limit where the heavy quarkonia are approximately point-like. We present a full next-to-leading order collinear factorization for the hard exclusive production of heavy mesons that retains the meson mass as well as full light-cone distribution amplitude. We compare the full NLO result with the special limits and estimate the errors due to potentially-large corrections from $\alpha_s(M)$ and $M^2/Q^2$ at this order.

papers.title: BPS baryonic tubes in chiral perturbation theory minimally coupled with electrodynamics and a novel crossover
papers.abstract: We derive a novel first-order BPS system (whose solutions are automatically solutions of the second-order field equations) in chiral perturbation theory (CPT) in $(3+1)$ dimensions. These BPS configurations describe baryonic tubes carrying a chiral current along the tubes themselves. Such baryonic tubes can be either homogeneous or modulated along the $z$-axis. We analyze the leading term in CPT, which is the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to electrodynamics. These exact solutions are qualitatively different from the available analytic description of baryonic tubes since, due to their BPS nature, the positions of the energy-density peaks can be arbitrary. In contrast (in the case of the known solutions in the literature), the energy-density peaks' positions are fixed. We compare these two types of baryonic configurations; the relevant parameter that determines which one is energetically favored is the baryonic charge density: for low densities, the old solutions are favorable, while for high densities these novel BPS tubes are energetically favored. The inclusion of the electromagnetic field (together with the corresponding back-reaction on the baryonic tubes) can also be treated analytically. We discuss the differences in the electromagnetic field distribution between the two regions (low and high baryonic density). The analysis of potential terms for the chiral field is detailed in Appendix B.

papers.title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
papers.abstract: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum. The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution. The two mesons exhibit qualitatively different light-cone structure, dictated by charge conjugation. The vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA, whose vanishing zeroth moment requires a normalization through its first moment. The decay constants obtained from local matrix elements and from the moments of the LCDAs agree, and approach predictions from nonrelativistic model as the fermion mass increases. For the relatively large masses considered in this work, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, showing that the mesons are dominated by their valence component. Our results demonstrate tensor networks as a practical route to light-cone distributions of ground-state as well as excited hadrons in low-dimensional gauge theories.

papers.title: The impact of phase transitions on dilepton production
papers.abstract: We calculate dielectron yields at beam energies relevant for the CBM experiment at FAIR and the STAR Beam Energy Scan. The production of intermediate mass dielectrons is expected to increase in presence of a phase transition due to the latent heat. In this work, we use the SMASH+vHLLE hybrid model to quantify this enhancement in two scenarios: with a toy equation of state consisting of the Bag Model and Hadron Resonance Gas, separated by a Maxwell-constructed transition; and with a more realistic equation of state containing a critical endpoint, based on the 3D Ising universality class. We confirm that the dilepton yield increases when the system passes through a first-order phase transition, by about 7% in the realistic scenario.

papers.title: Z boson production in lead-lead collisions: An investigation Utilizing MRW nuclear TMDs
papers.abstract: We investigate $Z$-boson production in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$ within the $k_t$-factorization framework, using four nuclear transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution (TMD) prescriptions, namely LO-MRW, VO-MRW, MVO-MRW, and MKMRW. The aim of this study is to examine how different ordering conditions and normalization treatments influence the theoretical description of this process. We calculate the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions using the parton-level KaTie event generator and compare the predictions with CMS measurements and collinear NLO calculations. This comparison allows us to assess the sensitivity of the predicted distributions to the choice of UPDF prescription.

papers.title: The relativistic BCS-BEC crossover in closed form: the cutoff as an effective range
papers.abstract: At zero temperature the mean-field potential of a Dirac fermion with a pairing gap contains one momentum integral, that of the sum of its two quasiparticle levels. We evaluate it in closed form from a geometric construction: the two levels are distances in a plane, and the momentum line is a finite arc of a fixed ellipse, along which the charge, the scalar density and the pair amplitude, summed over the modes, are combinations of Legendre's three elliptic integrals. As the upper limit of the momentum grows, the integral grows by a quartic term, a quadratic term and a logarithm with a known coefficient. The two powers are absorbed into a constant and into the coupling, and with all momenta integrated what remains is a finite combination of Legendre's integrals and the logarithm of one scale $\lambda$. The gap equation and the density of the relativistic BCS-BEC crossover follow in closed form. Once the coupling has been traded for the scattering length, $\lambda$ takes the place of the cutoff that the literature keeps as a third parameter. We show that it fixes the effective range of the channel of the pair: for a pair of Dirac fermions of mass $m$ with the pairing vertex $\gamma_5$, $r_e=-(4/\pi m)[\ln(2\lambda/m)-1]$. At low density and a fixed $k_Fr_e$ the crossover is that of the two-channel model of a Feshbach resonance with the same scattering length and effective range. In the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model the pion decay constant fixes $\lambda$, the effective range of the pion channel is $-8\pi f_\pi^{2}/(N_cM^{3})$, and the constituent mass $M$ of the quark is the one parameter that remains free.

papers.title: $QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ Quark System and Gauge/String Duality II: String Breaking
papers.abstract: This is the second of two companion papers in which we continue developing the construction of the fully heavy tetraquark system using the gauge/string duality. Here, we extend this construction to model $SU(3)$ gauge theory with two light flavors of equal mass. As an application, we analyze the two lowest Born-Oppenheimer potentials, both analytically and numerically, for rectangular and collinear geometries. Our analysis reveals several critical scales associated with string reconnection and breaking, as well as junction annihilation and pinching. In addition, we find that the string tension is universal, whereas the string breaking distance is not.

papers.title: Lightest $\Omega$-baryon systems with strangeness $-3$ and $-6$ within the framework of Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the binding energies and spatial properties of few-body $\Omega$-baryon systems with strangeness $S=-3$ and $S=-6$ using the configuration-space Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations. For the first time, microscopic Faddeev--Yakubovsky calculations are performed for the four- and five-body $\Omega NNN$, $\Omega NNNN$, and $\Omega\Omega NN$ systems. We employ HAL QCD and meson-exchange $\Omega N$ interactions, together with the HAL QCD $\Omega\Omega$ potential, and examine the effects of Coulomb interactions and spin--isospin configurations. The calculations predict substantial enhancement of binding with increasing baryon number, with the most strongly bound $\Omega NNNN$ configurations reaching approximately $60$~MeV and bound $\Omega\Omega NN$ states in the $S=-6$ sector. The results reveal pronounced spin dependence and compact few-body structures, with the $\Omega$ baryon preferentially localized near the center-of-mass. These findings provide new predictions for light multistrange nuclear systems and extend microscopic few-body calculations into the four- and five-body $\Omega$-baryon sectors.

papers.title: Softer charged-hadron spectra in Ne+Ne than in O+O collisions at the same multiplicity at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV
papers.abstract: Charged-hadron spectra measured by the ATLAS Collaboration in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV are compared at the same charged-particle multiplicity instead of at the same centrality, to test whether the shape of the transverse-momentum spectrum at a given multiplicity depends on the size of the colliding system. At equal multiplicity, Ne+Ne collisions have a lower mean transverse momentum $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ than O+O collisions. Without any spectral fit, the published $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ values give a Ne+Ne/O+O ratio of 0.9822 at 3-4% centrality, 6.6 standard deviations below unity even if the O+O systematic uncertainties are taken as uncorrelated between centrality classes. At $0.4 < p_{\rm T} < 2$ GeV the Ne+Ne spectrum is described by the O+O spectrum with the transverse-momentum axis compressed by a single stretch factor, $\lambda_{\rm Ne/O} = 0.969$ in the 3-4% class. It lies 9.5 or 3.3 standard deviations below unity, depending on whether the common part of the O+O systematic uncertainties cancels between centrality classes. This ordering is expected if Ne+Ne collisions have a larger transverse area at the same multiplicity and a larger area gives a softer spectrum. The softening decreases towards peripheral collisions and is the same at forward pseudorapidity. In central collisions the spectral shape follows the centrality class more closely than the multiplicity. The same procedure is tested in Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions.

papers.title: Hadronic and partonic composition of QCD matter across the crossover
papers.abstract: We construct a phenomenological equation of state of strongly interacting matter at zero chemical potentials that provides a unified description of lattice QCD thermodynamics in terms of hadronic and partonic degrees of freedom in the temperature range $T=100$-$510$ MeV. The hadronic phase is described by the quantum van der Waals hadron resonance gas, extended by excluded-volume repulsion between mesons, while the quark-gluon plasma is modeled as an ideal gas of quarks and gluons supplemented with a phenomenological interaction term proportional to $T^3$. The two regimes are connected by a smooth crossover switching function. We determine the four model parameters - the meson hard-core radius, the strength of the partonic interaction term, and two parameters of the switching function - by fitting to lattice QCD results for the trace anomaly. In this model, hadronic contributions remain significant up to about $200$ MeV, well above the QCD chiral crossover. We also quantify the crossing contributions generated by the temperature dependence of the switching function. The switching temperature and the hadronic and partonic contributions depend on the chosen equations of state and switching function. The lattice thermodynamic data do not uniquely determine the microscopic composition of QCD matter.

papers.title: Levy-shaped femtoscopic sources from an exact solution of relativistic hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: An important goal of high-energy physics is to better understand the spacetime structure of particle emitting sources created in heavy-ion collisions. For a fraction of a second, a special form of matter, the so-called quark-gluon plasma (QGP), is created, which can be examined with the toolkit of femtoscopy. With the measurement of correlation functions it was determined that L\'evy distributions describe the shape of hadron (pion) emission sources at freeze-out the most accurately; however, analytic solutions of hydrodynamics typically yield Gaussian sources, and power-law tails are usually attributed to the hadronic stage rather than to the fluid dynamics itself. In this article we showcase an exact solution of the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics, which aims to resolve this puzzle by providing L\'evy distributions directly from hydrodynamics. A detailed analysis reveals whether the predictions of this solution are in accordance with observations; in particular, the effective temperatures from angle-averaged transverse mass distributions and the femtoscopic radii from two-particle momentum correlation functions are analyzed.

papers.title: Nuclear Excitation by Inelastic Positron Scattering in Hydrogenlike $^{229}\mathrm{Th}^{89+}$ Ions
papers.abstract: We develop a relativistic theory of nuclear excitation by inelastic positron scattering (NEIPS) with nuclear hyperfine mixing (NHM) explicitly included and apply it to hydrogenlike $^{229}\mathrm{Th}^{89+}$ ions. The target ion is described by dressed hyperfine states, while the incident and outgoing positron continuum states are treated within a relativistic distorted-wave approach. We calculate hyperfine-resolved excitation cross sections for incident positron energies from $10^{2}$ to $10^{5}~\mathrm{eV}$. The cross sections increase strongly with the positron energy, with the $F_g=2\rightarrow F_e=2$ channel exhibiting the largest value. Comparison with NEIPS of the bare $^{229}\mathrm{Th}^{90+}$ nucleus shows that NHM enhances the excitation cross sections by about four orders of magnitude. These results demonstrate that NHM provides an efficient mechanism for enhancing NEIPS and broaden the range of nuclear excitation processes in which NHM plays a significant role.

papers.title: Total kinetic energy of fission fragments within time-dependent density functional theory: role of particle-number projection and collective deformations
papers.abstract: Time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations of fission fragment total kinetic energy (TKE), restricted to axially symmetric trajectories and a single symmetry-violating mean-field state, underestimate TKE by 10-20 MeV away from the most probable mass split. We reexamine this for $^{240}$Pu and $^{252}$Cf within relativistic TDDFT+BCS, combining particle-number projection (PNP) with an extended collective space including hexadecapole and non-axial deformations. Varying the pairing strength leaves the TKE essentially unchanged, but PNP converts each trajectory into a resolved TKE distribution over fragment mass, and the enlarged collective space is needed to reach the correct scission configurations. Together, these reproduce the empirical TKE mass dependence substantially better than standard calculations, indicating the discrepancy reflects missing symmetry restoration and configuration space rather than a deficient energy functional.

papers.title: Neural Network Potential Reconstruction from Phase Shifts in Resonant $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ Scattering
papers.abstract: We reconstruct a local, energy-independent effective potential for the narrow $D_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ from elastic phase shifts, using a Gaussian-enveloped neural parametrization coupled to a differentiable variable-phase calculation and checked by independent radial Schr\"odinger solvers. For the first resonance (below $2.5$ MeV LAB), the reconstruction gives a $90^\circ$ crossing at $1.001$ MeV LAB and a derivative width of $85$ keV LAB. The published Dubovichenko potential gives similar values with its original kinetic coefficient. Four reconstructions with adjustable range place the crossing within $5$ keV of one another while their central potentials span $47$ MeV. This spread illustrates the radial ambiguity of the inversion for the measured $D_{3/2}$ phases. The broad $P_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+\alpha$ serves as a benchmark for the same method.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
papers.abstract: Noise in quantum devices remains a major challenge for reliable quantum simulations, making quantum error mitigation an important tool for improving their accuracy. Machine learning-based quantum error mitigation (ML-QEM) provides a useful approach, but its performance depends on the training datasets and may produce reconstructed quantum states that are not physically valid. In this work, we introduce an ML-QEM framework that uses residual learning with convex projection to ensure that reconstructed density matrices satisfy physically valid density matrices. We study the effect of different training datasets and regression models using Haar-random and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansatz states. We compare the proposed approach with conventional ML-QEM, readout error mitigation, and zero-noise extrapolation. The method is tested on IBM quantum hardware for three- and four-qubit simulations of the bound $\Lambda$-deuteron and $\Lambda$-$\alpha$ hypernuclear systems, respectively. For the three-qubit system, ridge regression trained on VQE-ansatz states gives a ground-state energy of -0.134 MeV, close to the ideal value of -0.135 MeV, with a state fidelity of 0.999. For four-qubit system, kernel ridge regression gives ground-state energies of -3.014 and -3.045 MeV, with corresponding state fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998. These results show that physically constrained reconstruction, along with the choice of training datasets and regression models, can improve ML-QEM performance for the quantum simulations studied in this work.

papers.title: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding over Parametrized Many-Body Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: Many questions about interacting quantum systems ask which member of a Hamiltonian family $H(\mathbf{q})$ has the lowest ground-state energy, rather than for the ground state of one Hamiltonian. A pointwise scan answers this with one many-body solve per candidate. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) instead holds all $N_q$ candidates in a coherent register and searches them with a ground-energy threshold oracle, replacing $N_q$ solves by $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ coherent oracle calls. We identify static-field (Hubbard-Stratonovich) families as a broad class in which this minimum is a rigorous variational bound that the parent ground state does not reveal, and we make the oracle robust to imperfect ground-state preparation by fixed-point amplitude amplification. The measured search constant places the crossover against a pointwise quantum scan at $N_q \approx 220\xi^2$, where $\xi$ is the overhead of a coherent call. We test the search on realistic sd-shell (USDB) static quadrupole landscapes with up to $10^6$ grid points and on a Hubbard ring with competing orders. It pays where competing minima trap local descent, needing about four times fewer energy queries than multistart descent for oblate-prolate coexistence in $^{28}$Si, and not on smooth single-well landscapes. Circuit-level simulations validate the complete pipeline on a schematic model. The gain concerns the number of energy queries; any advantage of the quantum solver itself is separate.

papers.title: Differentiable emulation for high-dimensional Bayesian calibration of nuclear reaction models
papers.abstract: Bayesian calibration of a coupled-channel reaction model requires many expensive solves, and the likelihood gradients needed by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo are absent from most production solvers. I present DREAM (Differentiable Reduced-basis Emulator with Automatic gradients for Markov-chain inference), a strategy that makes a reduced model differentiable without differentiating the original solver: parameter-dependent operators and solution snapshots are exported offline, compressed by singular value decomposition, and reconstructed with differentiable operations, so each likelihood evaluation returns the observables together with the exact gradient of the emulated likelihood. The construction applies to discretized linear models whose parameter dependence admits a low-rank, low-dimensional operator representation, and direct solver calculations verify the reduced model at the posterior points where it is used. Applied to continuum-discretized coupled-channels calculations of $d$+$^{58}$Ni elastic scattering at 20 MeV, with eighteen central-potential parameters carried by twelve sampled coordinates, four chains yield 16000 retained samples in under an hour on one graphics processor, with an offline investment equivalent to about one thousand direct solves. Within the stated reaction model, continuum discretization, prior, and error assignment, the data determine the summed real and imaginary volume integrals as $772\pm13$ and $204\pm14$ MeV fm$^3$: the real integral lies 15% below the summed Koning-Delaroche reference and is stable under a global factor-of-two rescaling of the assigned experimental errors, while the proton-neutron decomposition of each sum is left undetermined.

papers.title: Coulomb-Induced $K^- pp$ Molecular State
papers.abstract: We study a new bound state in the three-body system consisting of an antikaon and two protons. The state is primarily induced by Coulomb interactions between the $K^-$ and the two protons, and is modified by strong $K^- p$ and $pp$ interactions. This spatially extended molecular state has binding energy and width that are of the order of keV, compared to the tens of MeV binding energy and width of the much-studied quasi-bound $K^- pp$ state caused primarily by strong interactions.
